items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: AC32-AC36 all implemented: config-axis + --codex-model flag (AC32), syntactic-allowlist-only validation with raise-before-launch (AC33, matching the architecture-review-simplified design), fable added unranked with a drift test across all 6 enumeration sites (AC34), --transport-note sources the effective model from run_codex_review's own returned dict, never a pre-fallback value (AC35), AC2 supersession documented in the ADR (AC36). No extra features beyond the spec (no live-catalog validator, per the rejected-alternative).

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: CodexReviewTransportError raised for caller mistakes (unknown role, bad timeout/max_retries, hostile model slug) before any subprocess launch; review_via_codex.py catches it and emits a structured error JSON instead of a traceback; OSError handled at every file read/write boundary (input files, schema load, canonical-path write, including a symlink guard).

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: The new model value is passed through _CODEX_MODEL_SLUG_PATTERN (anchored allowlist rejecting shell metacharacters/spaces) before ever reaching argv; env passed to the child stays the pre-existing explicit allowlist (untouched by this change); no secrets or tokens introduced.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: Tests assert on outcomes (returned dict shape, argv contents via index lookup, canonical file contents) not internals; hostile-input cases are parametrized; a real-subprocess E2E test proves the codex_plan_review vs codex_review config-key split end-to-end, not just via mocks.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: No loops, no DB/network calls beyond the existing single subprocess-per-attempt shape, unchanged by this diff.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: All touched/added files are under the 300-line cap (verified via git merge-base diff against origin/main after splitting codex_review_transport.py into codex_review_prompt.py/codex_review_roles.py and splitting two oversized test files); naming follows existing lib./tests conventions.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: Producer/consumer identified: shipwright_model_config.json (operator-edited) -> model_tier_config.load_model_config() (schema-validated). Round-trip tests exist for the new codex_review/codex_plan_review keys (test_model_tier_config_codex_and_fable.py) proving write-JSON -> load -> no spurious warning, satisfying touches_io_boundary.
